sl:
Preobrazba kompleksa bivše tovarne Mura v Murski Soboti
Projekt obravnava preobrazbo kompleksa nekdanje tovarne Mura v Murski Soboti ter njegovo vključevanje v mestno življenje. Kljub novim dejavnostim območje ostaja prostorsko razdrobljeno in zaradi železniške proge slabše povezano z mestnim središčem. Na podlagi teoretskih izhodišč ponovne rabe, referenčnih primerov ter zgodovinske in prostorske analize naloga razvija zasnovo njegove postopne preobrazbe. Predlog nadaljuje zgodovinsko mestno os z novo brvjo za pešce in kolesarje, ki povezuje park ob cerkvi, kreativni mladinski center v nekdanji upravni stavbi in parkirno hišo Park & Move. Zasnova poudarja ohranjanje obstoječe arhitekture, prilagodljivost rabe in izboljšanje dostopnosti. Izbrani posegi delujejo kot katalizatorji širšega oživljanja kompleksa, pri čemer povezave, javni prostori in novi programi ustvarjajo pogoje za nadaljnjo prenovo. Preobrazba je razumljena kot odprt proces, ki se razvija glede na potrebe uporabnikov.
en:
Transformation of the former Mura factory complex in Murska Sobota
The project addresses the transformation of the former Mura factory complex in Murska Sobota and its integration into the life of the city. Despite new activities, the area remains spatially fragmented and, because of the railway line, poorly connected to the city centre. Building on the theory of reuse, reference projects and a historical and spatial analysis, the thesis develops a concept for its gradual transformation. The proposal continues the historic city axis with a new pedestrian and cycling bridge that links the park by the church, a creative youth centre in the former administration building and the Park & Move car park. The design emphasises the preservation of existing architecture, flexibility of use and improved accessibility. Selected interventions act as catalysts for the wider revival of the complex, with connections, public spaces and new programmes creating the conditions for further renewal. The transformation is understood as an open process that evolves with the needs of its users.

Light
This project explores the possibilities of 3D printing beyond conventional layer-based fabrication. Through experimentation with custom G-code and continuous extrusion paths, the lamp investigates how the printing process itself can become a tool for design.
Rather than treating 3D printing solely as a means of reproducing predefined geometry, the project explores the relationship between material behaviour, toolpath generation, and the resulting form. The continuous deposition of material creates a woven, translucent structure that interacts with light, producing a distinctive texture and visual depth.
Developed through an iterative process of digital experimentation and physical prototyping, the lamp represents an ongoing exploration of computational design, material expression, and additive manufacturing.
sl:
Light
Projekt raziskuje možnosti 3D-tiska onkraj običajne izdelave po plasteh. Z eksperimentiranjem z lastno G-kodo in neprekinjenimi potmi ekstrudiranja svetilka raziskuje, kako lahko sam proces tiskanja postane orodje oblikovanja.
Namesto da bi 3D-tisk obravnaval zgolj kot sredstvo za reprodukcijo vnaprej določene geometrije, projekt raziskuje odnos med obnašanjem materiala, generiranjem poti orodja in nastalo obliko. Neprekinjeno nanašanje materiala ustvari tkano, prosojno strukturo, ki se odziva na svetlobo ter ustvarja značilno teksturo in vizualno globino.
Svetilka, razvita skozi iterativni proces digitalnega eksperimentiranja in fizičnega prototipiranja, predstavlja nadaljnje raziskovanje računalniškega oblikovanja, izraznosti materiala in aditivne proizvodnje.

en:
Oculus

Anja Markuš & David Ficko
Ponzano di Fermo is a picturesque village nestled in the rolling hills of the Marche region in central Italy. Located approximately 60 km south of Ancona and 30 km north of Ascoli Piceno. The town’s history dates back to at least 1059, with archaeological findings indicating habitation since the 4th century A.D. The town evolved around a castle and was influenced by various rulers over the centuries, including the Malatesta and Sforza families. The Madonna delle Cataste is a captivating and enigmatic site located in the countryside of Ponzano di Fermo. Constructed in the early 1920s, it stands as a testament to local legends and spiritual devotion. This Temple is a unique focal point of the project having both spiritual and architectural meaning to it. The octagonal shape with its impressive arche gives a cinematic as well as dramatic look, perfect for a stage backdrop. The teater is dramatical its fun, it's open to many interpretations as well as it being something that connected the people for generations and it will do so onward. In short this also means that it’s never ending. Another thing that is endless, is a circle which was also the shape of the first big theatres. On top of that it's also the symbol for unity as it brings us all together on equal footing no matter who we are or what we are we are all equal. Given the context of the area gave way for an interesting shape. The circle that embraces the central volume becomes the frame of the for the performance; it enhances the space as well as creates the boundary between the normal everyday world and the enchanting world of the performing arts. The theatre seats 131 people comfortably as well as giving space for people to stay in back if needed. All seats have a different perspective on the cemented stage as it follows the circular structure following the path that has been already given.
sl:
Oculus

Anja Markuš & David Ficko
Ponzano di Fermo je slikovita vas med valovitimi griči pokrajine Marke v osrednji Italiji, približno 60 km južno od Ancone in 30 km severno od Ascolija Piceno. Zgodovina kraja sega vsaj v leto 1059, arheološke najdbe pa pričajo o poselitvi že od 4. stoletja našega štetja. Kraj se je razvil okoli gradu, skozi stoletja pa so nanj vplivali različni vladarji, med njimi rodbini Malatesta in Sforza. Madonna delle Cataste je očarljivo in skrivnostno svetišče na podeželju Ponzana di Ferma. Zgrajeno v zgodnjih dvajsetih letih 20. stoletja, priča o lokalnih legendah in duhovni predanosti. Tempelj je osrednja točka projekta, saj ima tako duhovni kot arhitekturni pomen. Osmerokotna oblika z mogočnim lokom ustvarja filmski in dramatičen videz – popolno ozadje za oder. Gledališče je dramatično in zabavno, odprto mnogim interpretacijam, hkrati pa nekaj, kar ljudi povezuje že generacije in jih bo povezovalo tudi naprej. Skratka, nikoli se ne konča. Neskončen je tudi krog, ki je bil tudi oblika prvih velikih gledališč. Poleg tega je simbol enotnosti, saj nas vse postavi na enako raven – ne glede na to, kdo smo, smo vsi enaki. Kontekst prostora je narekoval zanimivo obliko. Krog, ki objema osrednji volumen, postane okvir predstave; poudari prostor in hkrati ustvari mejo med običajnim vsakdanjim svetom in očarljivim svetom uprizoritvenih umetnosti. Gledališče udobno sprejme 131 gledalcev, zadaj pa je po potrebi prostor tudi za stojišča. Vsak sedež ima drugačen pogled na betonski oder, saj sedeži sledijo krožni strukturi in že začrtani poti.

en:
Countryard
The architectural project focuses on designing an urban community in Čakovec, located along the Northern Bypass, that balances residential, educational, and public spaces. The plan includes 490 housing units for about 1,470 residents, with a land use ratio (FAR) of 1.28 and 24% site coverage. Various housing typologies, including townhouses, gallery blocks, and terraced buildings, ensure a diversity of living options.
The project’s identity is defined by the perimeter block layout, which provides clearly separated public and private spaces, improved microclimatic conditions, and efficient land use. Inner courtyards offer protection from noise and wind while creating green atriums, playgrounds, and communal areas, strengthening neighborhood connections and safety. The perimeter design ensures optimal sunlight exposure, improves energy efficiency, and increases the density and functionality of the urban fabric. A key feature of the project is its strong integration with green infrastructure, emphasizing sustainable development and high quality of life. A central green axis crosses the settlement, forming a network of parks, green courtyards, and stormwater retention elements that enhance biodiversity and enable natural water management. Green parking areas and noise barriers further contribute to the eco-friendly design.
Public spaces are designed to foster social interaction. Multipurpose open areas support events and gatherings, reinforcing community identity. The educational zone includes a high school, youth center, and student dormitory, strategically placed to ensure safe pedestrian routes. The architectural concept prioritizes high living standards: glazed northern façades reduce noise and allow controlled ventilation; ground-floor apartments have private gardens, while green courtyards offer shared recreational spaces.

mentors: Assoc. Prof. Uroš Lobnik, udia & Assist. Žiga Kreševič
sl:
Countryard
Arhitekturni projekt se osredotoča na zasnovo mestne soseske v Čakovcu ob severni obvoznici, ki uravnoteži stanovanjske, izobraževalne in javne prostore. Načrt vključuje 490 stanovanjskih enot za približno 1.470 prebivalcev, s faktorjem izrabe (FAR) 1,28 in 24-odstotno pozidanostjo. Različne stanovanjske tipologije – vrstne hiše, galerijski bloki in terasaste stavbe – zagotavljajo raznolike možnosti bivanja.
Identiteto projekta določa zasnova obodnih karejev, ki zagotavlja jasno ločene javne in zasebne prostore, boljše mikroklimatske pogoje in učinkovito rabo zemljišča. Notranja dvorišča nudijo zaščito pred hrupom in vetrom ter ustvarjajo zelene atrije, igrišča in skupne prostore, ki krepijo sosedske vezi in varnost. Obodna zasnova zagotavlja optimalno osončenost, izboljšuje energetsko učinkovitost ter povečuje gostoto in funkcionalnost mestnega tkiva. Ključna značilnost projekta je tesna povezanost z zeleno infrastrukturo, s poudarkom na trajnostnem razvoju in visoki kakovosti bivanja. Osrednja zelena os prečka naselje in tvori mrežo parkov, zelenih dvorišč in elementov za zadrževanje meteorne vode, ki povečujejo biotsko raznovrstnost in omogočajo naravno upravljanje z vodo. K okolju prijazni zasnovi prispevajo tudi zelena parkirišča in protihrupne ograje.
Javni prostori so zasnovani tako, da spodbujajo druženje. Večnamenske odprte površine omogočajo dogodke in srečanja ter krepijo identiteto skupnosti. Izobraževalno območje vključuje srednjo šolo, mladinski center in študentski dom, umeščene tako, da zagotavljajo varne peš poti. Arhitekturni koncept daje prednost visokemu bivalnemu standardu: zastekljene severne fasade zmanjšujejo hrup in omogočajo nadzorovano prezračevanje; pritlična stanovanja imajo zasebne vrtove, zelena dvorišča pa ponujajo skupne prostore za rekreacijo.

mentorji: izr. prof. Uroš Lobnik, udia & asist. Žiga Kreševič

Peja culture pavilion Buildner competition
Anja Markuš & David Ficko

The international competition invited ideas for the renewal of a historic space in the centre of Peja, Kosovo. The aim was to connect a 15th-century fountain and a new pavilion with the existing urban environment – to create a place that respects the city’s cultural heritage while offering new possibilities for the community.

Stanovanjska soseska ZELENA VAS MARIBOR se nahaja južno od Puhove ulice na Pobrežju, na vzhodnem robu mesta Maribor. Soseska leži v območju pretežno enostanovanjske gradnje, ki jo na zahodu ob prometnici prekinjajo večji trgovski in industrijski objekti. Na severu območje meji na nekdanjo pobreško deponijo.

Na severu območja so postavljene stavbe s pretežno javnim programom, ki služijo kot zvočna bariera med vpadnico in stanovanjskim delom območja. Med severnim in južnim predelom se nahaja linijski park, ki ponuja različne možnosti za sprostitev, rekreacijo in igro ter povezuje stanovanjski del s centralnimi dejavnostmi( šola, trgovina, biznis...) na vzhodu območja. Bloki ob parku so postavljeni v cikcak vzorcu, s čimer se zagotavlja odpiranje različnih pogledov ter “zajedanje” parka v območje stanovanj. Med bloki se tvorijo poljavni prostori, namenjeni igri, druženju, rekreaciji stanovalcev. Stavbe so različnih višin, od P+2 do P+7, večstanovanjski objekti se gibljejo med P+4 ter P+6. Na vzhodu območja se tvori manjši trg s tgovsko-poslovnim objektom, kulturnim centrom za druženje in povezovanje stanovalcev ter osnovno šolo. Na vzhodnem robu je predvidena zelena gozdnata površina, ki predstavlja zvočno bariero za centralne dejavnosti.
en:
The ZELENA VAS MARIBOR (Green Village Maribor) residential neighbourhood lies south of Puhova ulica in Pobrežje, on the eastern edge of Maribor. It sits in an area of mostly single-family houses, interrupted to the west, along the main road, by larger retail and industrial buildings. To the north, the site borders the former Pobrežje landfill.

In the north of the site are buildings with mainly public programmes, which act as a noise barrier between the arterial road and the residential part of the area. Between the northern and southern parts runs a linear park that offers different opportunities for relaxation, recreation and play, and connects the housing with the central activities (school, shops, offices...) in the east. The blocks along the park are arranged in a zigzag pattern, opening up varied views and letting the park “bite” into the residential area. Between the blocks, semi-public spaces form for play, socialising and recreation. The buildings range in height from G+2 to G+7, with the apartment buildings between G+4 and G+6. In the east, a small square forms with a retail and office building, a cultural centre where residents can meet and connect, and a primary school. Along the eastern edge, a green wooded area is planned as a noise barrier for the central activities.

sl: Objekt združuje atletski center ter hotel namenjen športnikom. Objekt je podkleten, v kleti se nahaja atletska dvorana s progo za tek na 100m ter ustrezna oprema za skok v višino. Garderobe se nahajajo v pritličju, kjer najdemo tudi savno ter prostor namenjen fizioterapiji ter zdravniškim pregledom. V prvem NADSTROPJU so prostori namenjeni medijem ter sejna soba za razne seminarje oz. predavanja. Objekt ima stekleno fasado, ki nam nudi lepe poglede iz objekta ter hkrati objektu daje lahkotnost ter transparentnost.
en: The building combines an athletics centre and a hotel for athletes. The basement houses an indoor athletics hall with a 100 m running track and equipment for the high jump. The changing rooms are on the ground floor, which also has a sauna and rooms for physiotherapy and medical examinations. The first floor contains rooms for the media and a conference room for seminars and lectures. The glass façade offers fine views out of the building while giving it lightness and transparency.

sl:
GENTRIFIKACIJA?
Slovar slovenskega knjižnega jezika termin gentrifikacija opredeljuje kot:
»spreminjanje pretežno bivalnih mestnih predelov z lokalnim prebivalstvom s pozidavo, prenovo v predele s turistično, storitveno namembnostjo višjega razreda.« [1] Besedo je skovala ter prvič uporabila britanska sociologinja Ruth Glass, ko je v Londonu opazovala preseljevanje srednjega, premožnejšega sloja (»the gentry«) v revnejše predele delavskega razreda. Definicja besede, ki jo najdemo v SSKJ je v skladu z opažanji Glassove:
»Ena za drugo so mnoge četrti delavskega razreda v Londonu zasedli srednji razredi, zgornji in spodnji. Zanikrne, skromne hiše in koče z dvema prostoroma zgoraj in dvema spodaj so bile prevzete, ko so jim potekle najemne pogodbe, in so postale elegantna, draga bivališča. (...) Ko se ta proces 'gentrifikacije' začne v neki četrti, poteka hitro, dokler niso vsi ali večina prvotnih prebivalcev delavskega razreda izpodrinjeni, in se celoten socialni značaj četrti spremeni.«
[2, Glass, 1964, xviii – xix]
Sharon Zukin, profesorica emerita sociologije, je analizirala spreminjanje
predela SoHo v New Yorku. V večinoma delavski predel mesta so se začeli priseljevati umetniki, ki so si v starejših, cenovno dostopnih hišah začeli urejati studie in stanovanja. [3] Umetniki so v sosesko prinesli »kulturni kapital«[4], kar je pritegnilo višje družbene razrede, ki so s časom zaradi večje kupne moči umetnike izrinili. Po Bordieu se kulturni kapital nanaša na neekonomske vire, kot so znanje, veščine, poznavanje norm in vrednot ter kulturne dobrine. [5, 1986]
Gary Bridge, socialni urbani geograf, omenja, da sta distirbucija in kroženje kulturnega kapitala ključni sili, ki vplivata na usodo mest v metropolitanskih območjih po svetu, predvsem v okviru sprememb, ki jih povzroča gentrifikacija.[6, v Velkavrh, 26]
Neil Smith, geografski teoretik, poudarja, da je gentrifikacija del širšega procesa urbanega razvoja. Ne vidi težav v povpraševanju novega srednjega razreda, temveč v ponudbi na nempremičninskem trgu. Pudarja, da je ključni dejavnik gentrifikacije vse večja razlika med potencialno vrednostjo zemljiščne rente in kapitalizirano vrednostjo zemljišča.  Ustvarjeno rentno vrzel izkoriščajo nepremičninski agenti in razvijalci tako, da najprej načrtno razvrednotijo
sosesko, nato pa jo za dobiček obnovijo. [7, Smith v Hekič]
Hackworth gentrifikacijo razloži kot »produkcijo prostora za postopoma vse bolj premožne uporabnike« [6, v Velkavrh, 27] Sklepamo lahko, da je ključna razlika med gentrifikacijo nekega območja in prenovo ali revitalizacijo v tem, da gentrifikacija zmeraj vodi do izrinjenja ali razpada prvotne skupnosti. Zaradi zvišanega standarda so prvotni prebivalci primorani zapustiti gentrificirano območje.

GENTRIFIKACIJA V LJUBLJANI?
Kritični geograf David Harvey, ki je zagovornik Lefebvrejevega koncepta »Pravica do mesta«, spremembo v načinu upravljanja mest, v okoliščinah neoliberalizma, opiše kot pomik od menedžerske kulture k podjetniški. Staro mesto je bilo organizirano okoli tovarne, novo mesto, ki je kot podjetje, pa je organizirano okoli porabe. [8] Mesta se danes vse bolj ukvarjajo s tem kako privabiti čim več kapitala ter porabnikov. Zukin ugotavlja: »Koncept se je preselil od kvalitete ljudi h kvaliteti stvari in nedavno h kvaliteti izkušnje.«[9]

Prebivalec mesta postaja hkrati turist, ki mesto doživlja in predvsem troši denar, kvaliteta življenja pa se prodaja kot turistična znamenitost.[8] Ploštajner poudarja, da se prenova Ljubljanjskega mestenga središča ravna po tej podjetniški strategiji: »Še pred desetletjem smo se lahko zgražali nad tem, da središče mesta propada, ker se je poraba preselila v BTC, zdaj pa smo priča oživljanju mestnega središča, ki pa je postalo zgolj premišljeno in v skladu z načeli »novega urbanizma« urejeno trgovsko središče.«[8]
Podobno se dogaja z javnimi prostori, postajajo prostori spektakla.
»V družbah, kjer vladajo moderne produkcijske razmere, se celotno življenje kaže kot neizmerno kopičenje spektaklov.« [10, Debord] Debord spektakel razlaga kot »medosebni družbeni odnos, katerega posrednik so podobe.«[11]
Ploštajner opisuje proces nastajanja prostora spektakla:»S trgov se umikajo parkirišča in na njih rastejo koncertni odri, na ulicah ni več avtomobilov, ampak stojnice, nabrežja niso več prazna, temveč polna lokalov.«[8]
Če so včasih mesta predstavljala zatočišče najbolj propulzivnih, ustvarjalnih, inovativnih, tudi čudnih posameznikov in skupnosti, gentrifikacija pomeni ravno obratno. Povzroči izrinjenje ravno teh posameznikov in skupnosti, mesta si več ne morejo privoščiti. Prostor rojevanja novih trendov, kulturnih gibanj in inovacije, postane spektakel kulture, dobrin in storitev. Vsakdanje meščansko življenje, se je primorano umakniti spektaklu, ki mesto spremeni v stroj za ustvarjanje zasebnih dobičkov. [12]

KAPITAL UBIJA?
Prenova nekdanje tovarne Rog je vzbudila bujen odziv. Skvoterji so bili pred prenovo iz tovarne nasilno izgnani, njihova oprema pa uničena. Anonimna uporabnica, ki je od leta 2002 aktivno dejavna v boju izbrisanih kot raziskovalka, aktivistka, podpornica in sopotnica, zapisuje: »Ob tem brez svojega političnega doma niso ostali le izbrisani in migrantska skupnost, ampak so brez prostorov in svojih sanj ostali številni kolektivi na področju športa, cirkusa, glasbe, plesa, kreativnega pisanja, kvir-anarhističnega samoorganiziranja, gledališča, skupnostnega kuhanja in prehranjevanja, solidarnostnih in prijateljskih vezi, uničen je bil tako skejt park kot cirkusarna, koncertna dvorana, gore knjig, računalniška oprema in tako dalje. Kot je dejal Irfan Beširović – uničevanje prostorov, opreme in arhiva, vključno s transparenti, plakati, zapisniki skupščin in tako dalje spominja na zažiganje knjig v totalitarnih režimih.« [13]
Ideja prvotne skupine Temp, ki je tovarno zasedla leta 2006, je bila vzpostavitev prostora ustvarjalnosti, ki ga je takrat v mestu primanjkovalo. »Kmalu se vzpostavi nov prostor za dialog, sodelovanje, neposredno demokracijo, skupščino – z namenom ustvariti mesto inovacij in novih načinov raziskovanja.« [14, Grabar] Ideja, ki je oblikovala Avtonomno tovarno Rog že pred prenovo, se je po evikciji in prenovi ponovno udejanjila v Centru Rog. Obstoječi uporabniki so bili z območja izrinjeni, prostor pa je postal del podjetniškega mesta, ki je organizirano okoli porabe. Avtentičnost Avtonomne tovarne Rog je nadomestil prostor spektakla kulture, dobrin in storitev.
Projekt z arhitekturnega vidika predstavlja dober primer prenove obstoječega stavbnega tkiva. Arhitektura je zadržana, a hkrati kvalitetna. Boris Bežan, arhitekt, ki vodi studio BAX, je v intervjuju zapisal: » Želimo si, da bi objekt zares zaživel. Stavba je dovolj prilagodljiva, da so v njej mogoči kakršnikoli programi. Predvsem mlajša populacija želi prostore, ki omogočajo demokratično vključevanje posameznikov. Upam, da jim bo Rog namenil vsaj del prostorov: da bodo našli svojo delavnico, kjer bodo lahko počeli vse, kar bi običajno počeli v garaži staršev. Želim si, da bi v Rogu našli dopolnilo tistemu, kar pogrešajo v vsakdanjem življenju. «[15]

»Kot ni bilo mogoče izbrisati ljudi, tudi ideje Avtonomne tovarne Rog ni mogoče ne izbrisati, ne uničiti. Prostori so uničeni, ideje in ljudje smo preživeli. Čeprav je bil uničen velik del arhiva izbrisanih, zgodovino tega boja, ki je tudi boj proti gentrifikaciji, predajamo prihajajočim generacijam.«[13]

Gentrifikacija predstavlja velik izziv nadaljnemu razvoju urbanih območij. Dokler se mesta razvijajo v smeri porabe in spektakla, lahko hitro podležejo gentrifikaciji in postanejo prostor za vedno bolj premožne uporabnike. Vskaršna prenova ali revitalizacija mestnega tkiva mora biti dobro premišljena, tako da gradi avtentičnost mesta in ne ruši obstoječe skupnosti. Če prenova tovarne Rog predstavlja kvaliteten primer prenove, pa sodelovanje investitorja z obstoječimi uporabniki predstavlja ravno nasprotno. Namesto participativnega oblikovanja je prišlo do nasilne evikcije ter izrinjenja. Kapital ubija? V primeru Roga je odgovor pritridilen. Kapital, ki za nekatere ubija, za druge gradi. Namesto da se sprašujemo, ali kapital ubija, bi se morali vprašati, ali kapital resnično prispeva k izgradnji skupnosti.

en:
GENTRIFICATION?
The Dictionary of Standard Slovene defines the term gentrification as:
“the transformation of predominantly residential urban districts with a local population, through new construction and renovation, into districts with tourist and higher-end service uses.” [1] The word was coined and first used by the British sociologist Ruth Glass while observing the movement of the middle, wealthier class (“the gentry”) into poorer working-class districts of London. The definition found in the dictionary is in line with Glass’s observations:
“One by one, many of the working-class quarters of London have been invaded by the middle classes – upper and lower. Shabby, modest mews and cottages – two rooms up and two down – have been taken over, when their leases have expired, and have become elegant, expensive residences. (...) Once this process of ‘gentrification’ starts in a district, it goes on rapidly until all or most of the original working-class occupiers are displaced, and the whole social character of the district is changed.”
[2, Glass, 1964, xviii – xix]
Sharon Zukin, professor emerita of sociology, analysed the transformation of SoHo in New York. Artists began moving into this mostly working-class part of the city, setting up studios and apartments in older, affordable buildings. [3] The artists brought “cultural capital” [4] to the neighbourhood, which attracted higher social classes who, over time and with greater purchasing power, pushed the artists out. According to Bourdieu, cultural capital refers to non-economic resources such as knowledge, skills, familiarity with norms and values, and cultural goods. [5, 1986]
Gary Bridge, a social and urban geographer, notes that the distribution and circulation of cultural capital are key forces shaping the fate of cities in metropolitan areas around the world, particularly in the context of the changes brought about by gentrification. [6, in Velkavrh, 26]
Neil Smith, a geographical theorist, stresses that gentrification is part of a wider process of urban development. He sees the problem not in the demand of a new middle class but in the supply side of the property market. He argues that the key driver of gentrification is the growing gap between the potential ground rent and the capitalised value of land. This rent gap is exploited by estate agents and developers, who first deliberately devalue a neighbourhood and then renovate it for profit. [7, Smith in Hekič]
Hackworth explains gentrification as “the production of space for progressively more affluent users” [6, in Velkavrh, 27]. We can conclude that the key difference between the gentrification of an area and its renovation or revitalisation is that gentrification always leads to the displacement or disintegration of the original community. Because of the raised standard, the original residents are forced to leave the gentrified area.

GENTRIFICATION IN LJUBLJANA?
The critical geographer David Harvey, an advocate of Lefebvre’s concept of “the right to the city”, describes the change in how cities are governed under neoliberalism as a shift from a managerial to an entrepreneurial culture. The old city was organised around the factory; the new city, run like a company, is organised around consumption. [8] Today, cities are increasingly concerned with how to attract as much capital and as many consumers as possible. Zukin observes: “The concept has shifted from the quality of people to the quality of things and, more recently, to the quality of experience.” [9]

The city dweller becomes at the same time a tourist who experiences the city and, above all, spends money, while quality of life is sold as a tourist attraction. [8] Ploštajner points out that the renovation of Ljubljana’s city centre follows this entrepreneurial strategy: “Only a decade ago we could be outraged that the city centre was decaying because consumption had moved to BTC; now we are witnessing the revival of the centre, which has, however, become nothing more than a shopping centre, carefully arranged according to the principles of ‘new urbanism’.” [8]
Something similar is happening to public spaces: they are becoming spaces of spectacle.
“In societies where modern conditions of production prevail, all of life presents itself as an immense accumulation of spectacles.” [10, Debord] Debord describes the spectacle as “a social relationship between people that is mediated by images.” [11]
Ploštajner describes how a space of spectacle comes into being: “Car parks are disappearing from the squares and concert stages are growing in their place; there are no longer cars in the streets but market stalls; the riverbanks are no longer empty but full of bars.” [8]
If cities were once a refuge for the most driven, creative, innovative and even strange individuals and communities, gentrification means exactly the opposite. It displaces precisely those individuals and communities, who can no longer afford the city. A place where new trends, cultural movements and innovation are born becomes a spectacle of culture, goods and services. Everyday urban life is forced to give way to a spectacle that turns the city into a machine for generating private profit. [12]

CAPITAL KILLS?
The renovation of the former Rog factory provoked a strong reaction. Before the renovation, the squatters were violently evicted from the factory and their equipment destroyed. An anonymous user, active since 2002 in the struggle of the Erased as a researcher, activist, supporter and companion, writes: “It was not only the Erased and the migrant community that were left without their political home; numerous collectives working in sport, circus, music, dance, creative writing, queer-anarchist self-organisation, theatre, community cooking and eating, and bonds of solidarity and friendship lost their spaces and their dreams. The skate park was destroyed, as were the circus hall, the concert hall, mountains of books, computer equipment and so on. As Irfan Beširović said, the destruction of spaces, equipment and archives, including banners, posters, assembly minutes and so on, is reminiscent of book burnings in totalitarian regimes.” [13]
The idea of the original group Temp, which occupied the factory in 2006, was to create a space for creativity, which the city lacked at the time. “Soon a new space for dialogue, cooperation, direct democracy and assembly was established – with the aim of creating a place of innovation and new ways of exploring.” [14, Grabar] The idea that had shaped the Rog Autonomous Factory before the renovation was realised once again, after the eviction and renovation, in the Rog Centre. The existing users were pushed out of the area, and the space became part of the entrepreneurial city organised around consumption. The authenticity of the Rog Autonomous Factory was replaced by a space of spectacle of culture, goods and services.
Architecturally, the project is a good example of the renovation of existing building fabric. The architecture is restrained yet of high quality. Boris Bežan, the architect who leads studio BAX, said in an interview: “We want the building to truly come alive. It is flexible enough to accommodate any kind of programme. Younger people in particular want spaces that allow individuals to take part democratically. I hope Rog will give them at least some of its spaces: that they will find their workshop there, where they can do everything they would normally do in their parents’ garage. I hope they will find in Rog what is missing from their everyday lives.” [15]

“Just as it was not possible to erase people, the idea of the Rog Autonomous Factory cannot be erased or destroyed either. The spaces have been destroyed; the ideas and we, the people, have survived. Although a large part of the archive of the Erased was destroyed, we pass the history of this struggle – which is also a struggle against gentrification – on to the generations to come.” [13]

Gentrification is a major challenge for the future development of urban areas. As long as cities develop in the direction of consumption and spectacle, they can quickly succumb to gentrification and become spaces for ever more affluent users. Any renovation or revitalisation of the urban fabric must be carefully considered, so that it builds the authenticity of the city rather than destroying the existing community. While the renovation of the Rog factory is a high-quality example of renovation, the investor’s cooperation with the existing users represents the very opposite. Instead of participatory design, there was violent eviction and displacement. Does capital kill? In the case of Rog, the answer is yes. Capital that kills for some builds for others. Rather than asking whether capital kills, we should ask whether capital truly contributes to building community.
